column1: # *** THE ELDEST SALVANACH SON, HIS WIFE AND HIS SON - FamilySearch, 20 September 2026. ***
# Run to settle one thing: whether the Gilberto Lerena who landed off the CAP. NORTE on 27 February
# 1928 with a son of the same name is GILBERTO LERENA SALVANACH, born Montevideo 1878.
# It did not settle it. It did something better than a guess: *** the son the identification needed
# turned out to exist. *** That is a prediction meeting a record, and it is not the same as proof.
# Searched: surname LERENA, forename GILBERTO, Argentina, births 1875-1882. 63 results.
# *** The rendered "(0)" was there again *** - the count read zero on first load and 63 four seconds
# later. This archive has been caught by that before and reads twice as a matter of habit.
*** HIS MARRIAGE NAMES THE BRIDE, AND THIS ARCHIVE NEVER HAD HER ***
column2: Gilberto Lerena, groom, born *** 1878 "Rep. Oriental" ***, parents Gilberto Lerena and Julia Salvanach. Married *** 19 May 1906, Nuestra Senora del Pilar, Recoleta ***. Spouse: *** CIPRIANA SAENS PENA *** (indexed also "Cepriana Saenz Pena").
column3: Argentina, Capital Federal, Catholic Church Records, 1640-1978
column4: *** A NEW PERSON, and a surname worth noticing. *** The register carried this marriage with no bride at all. SAENZ PENA is a name that runs through Argentine public life in exactly these years - *** no relationship to either president is asserted or looked for ***, and the surname is not rare enough to carry one.

column1: *** AND THEY HAD A SON NAMED GILBERTO ***
column2: Gilberto Lerena, *** father ***, spouse "Cepriana Saenz Pena", child *** "Gilberto de Jesus del Corazon" *** (the index bleeds "Aires" into the surname field from the place).
column3: Argentina, Capital Federal, Catholic Church Records, 1640-1978
column4: *** THIS IS THE SON THE 1928 IDENTIFICATION PREDICTED. *** The CEMLA arrival has Gilberto b.1879 travelling with a son Gilberto, *** estudiante ***, aged twelve. Yesterday that son was a curiosity. Today he is in a parish index, from a marriage of 1906.

column1: *** BUT HIS BIRTH YEAR IS NOT INDEXED, SO THE TEST STILL FAILS ***
column2: A second search - LERENA, GILBERTO, Argentina, *** births 1910-1920 *** - returns 10 records and *** none of them is this child ***. The birth filter demonstrably works: it cut 63 to 10.
column4: *** SO 1916 IS UNCONFIRMED AND THE PAIR STAYS UNMERGED. *** The son exists; his age does not. An identification that rests on a name and a year still rests on a name and a year.

column1: *** HIS ARGENTINE NATIONALITY IS NOW ON A RECORD, NOT AN INFERENCE ***
column2: Military service *** March 1922, Distrito Militar 2, Argentina ***; birth *** 1878, Montevideo, Uruguay ***; parents Lerena and Julia Salvanach. A second entry gives *** Montecarlo, Misiones ***.
column4: *** A MONTEVIDEO-BORN MAN CARRIED ON AN ARGENTINE MILITARY DISTRICT ROLL. *** That is what the CEMLA passenger's "ARGENTINE" requires, and the register's "Uruguayan/Argentine" is now documented rather than assumed.

column1: *** AND THE 1895 INDEX EXPLAINS THE TABLE THAT WAS WRONG ***
column2: Searching the 1895 census returns the household of Seccion 21, Subdivision 15 as *** Gilberto 1854, Maria E. C. 1869, Maria Luisa 1880, Carlos A. 1884, Raul A. 1886, Maria E. 1890 *** - and *** NOT the seventeen-year-old ***, who is indexed under *** SALVANACH ***, not Lerena.
column4: *** THIS IS WHY /argentina/ CARRIED A TABLE OF NINE FOR SIX DAYS. *** It was built from this index, and the index files the eldest son under his mother's surname. The schedule has sixteen lines. Corrected 20 September; recorded here because the next person to build a table from an index deserves the warning.

column1: *** NO NEW CHILDREN. THE REGISTER ALREADY HAD THEM ALL ***
column2: The search returns Gilberto (1854) as father of *** Maria Carlota, Horacio Alfredo, Luis Felipe, Cesar Alberto, Raul and Carlos ***.
column4: *** ALL SIX ARE ALREADY IN THE REGISTER *** under LERENA Salvanach. Checked name by name before writing, because this archive added a duplicate of Dominga Llerena on the day it built a gate against duplicates.
